extracted.intended_audience: readers and commenters on The A.V. Club (general public / site community)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for participating in The A.V. Club’s online community via comments, including what behavior/content is acceptable, how to contact staff, and where to send tips or publicity inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall tone: intelligence and wit
rubrics_metrics.description: We strive to cover pop culture with intelligence and wit, and we assume that’s what brought you here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abusive/offensive/obscene posts simply don’t contribute to that goal. Aim for commentary that reflects intelligence/wit rather than raw abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: No flagrant attacks on commenters, staff, or subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Flagrant attacks on other commentators, staffers, or interview / review subjects, particularly aggressive, insulting posts with no other point to make, are unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Unacceptable example: “You’re a dick!”
Acceptable example: “Only a dick would watch Con Air six times in a row!”
Better example: “You watched Con Air six times?! You should’ve taken IQ tests before and after to see how it affected you.”
(Encourages making a point or humor rather than gratuitous insult.)

rubrics_metrics.name: No offensive commentary on appearance or sexual commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Offensive commentary on interview / review subjects, including but not limited to ad hominem thoughts on how they look, how they might smell, and exactly what you’d like to do to them in bed, is unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hate on their work all you want, but attacking them for their appearance is childish, and providing detailed commentary on your sexual reaction to them is icky. (Metaphor: if you did that at our party at our house, you wouldn’t be invited back.)

rubrics_metrics.name: No racist, homophobic, or sexist remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Racist, homophobic, or sexist remarks are unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t assume that everyone else gets your sarcasm, irony, over-the-top tone, etc. Attack comments don’t get a free pass just because you “didn’t really mean it.”

rubrics_metrics.name: No blatant trolling
rubrics_metrics.description: Blatant trolling is listed among behaviors the site finds unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid posting solely to provoke, derail discussion, or inflame other commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: No blatant plugs for your own website
rubrics_metrics.description: Blatant plugs for your own website are unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use comment threads as advertisement space for your own site or content.

rubrics_metrics.name: No offensive images or GIFs
rubrics_metrics.description: Offensive images or GIFs are unacceptable in comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual content should not be abusive, obscene, or otherwise offensive to the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community enforcement: report offensive behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: We can’t be everywhere at once. You can help us maintain the quality of our community. If you see someone behaving offensively in the comments, contact us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided contact channels to report violations so moderators/staff can address them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be passionate but be kind; remember the human
rubrics_metrics.description: Be passionate, but be kind. Learn from each other. And remember there is an actual human being on the other end of the line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comments work best when people follow this ethos—engage critically but respectfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to contact / where to send tips and publicist inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific contact addresses are provided for tips, AVQ&A suggestions, and publicists (books, games, music).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate email for your purpose (e.g., general tips, AVQ&A questions, books publicists, games publicists, music publicists) rather than posting such items in comment threads.
